headline: The Electrician Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet customers, give numbers and times, describe jobs, ask questions and make polite requests in Spanish, and start Electrician Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Pronounce Spanish vowels and key sounds and greet a customer at the door.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr, the written accent, and everyday greetings

words.note: Vowels are short and clean: a = 'ah', e = 'eh'.
ch sounds like English 'church'.
j is a strong breathy h, like 'ha'.
ll sounds like English y. It also means 'key'.
rr is a rolled r. Tap your tongue twice.
The accent mark means stress the last syllable: con-ex-IÓN.
u sounds like 'oo'.
j again: tra-BA-jo.
i sounds like 'ee'.
ñ sounds like 'ny' in 'canyon'.
Use buenos días until noon.
Usted is formal. Use it with customers.

lessons.speaking: Greet a customer at the door, say you are the electrician, say it is nice to meet them, and ask how they are.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say numbers, clock times and the units of electrical work, like feet, volts and amps.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and work units: feet, inches, volts, amps, gauge

words.note: Plural: los pies. Common for wire length in the US.
Many workers also say el volt.
Many workers also say el amp.
Wire size, like calibre 12.

words.en: It's 100 feet of wire, according to the plan.
words.es: Son 100 pies de cable, según el plano.

words.en: The power outage is from 9:00 to 11:00.
words.es: El corte de luz es de 9:00 a 11:00.

words.note: Read the number from the label. Never guess it.

words.en: The roll has 250 feet, according to the label.
words.es: El rollo tiene 250 pies, según la etiqueta.

words.note: Use son las for most hours, but es la 1:00 for one o'clock.

lessons.speaking: Tell a tenant when the power will be off: say the start time, the end time, and how many hours it lasts.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what things are and where they are, and whether they are safe, using ser and estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what something is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Mexican / US usage for a circuit or light that is on.

words.en: The panel is in the garage.
words.es: El panel está en el garaje.
words.note: estar: location.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.en: The floor is wet; it isn't safe.
words.es: El piso está mojado; no es seguro.

words.note: ser: who or what someone is.

words.en: It's dangerous to touch it if it's on.
words.es: Es peligroso tocarlo si está prendido.

lessons.speaking: Tell an apprentice where the panel is, say whether the switch is off or on, and warn that a wet floor or damaged wire is not safe.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, what there is, what you need and want, and what has to be done.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: Always plural in Spanish.
Standard job usage in the US.
US Spanish for pickup or work truck.

words.en: I have a ladder in the truck.
words.es: Tengo una escalera en la troca.

words.en: There's a problem in the panel.
words.es: Hay un problema en el panel.
words.note: hay means 'there is' and 'there are'.

words.en: I want to see the panel.
The breaker has to be turned off first.
words.es: Hay que apagar el breaker primero.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: 'it is necessary to'.

lessons.speaking: Tell an apprentice which tools you have, which you need, and one thing that has to be done before you start work.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do, and what you can do.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, poder

words.note: Also used for the supply store.

words.en: I'm going to the hardware store.
words.note: ir: voy, vas, va, vamos, van.

words.en: We're going to the job site at 7:00.
words.es: Vamos a la obra a las 7:00.

words.en: I'm going to do the test.
words.note: ir a + infinitive: a plan.

words.en: Tomorrow we're going to ask for the permit.
words.es: Mañana vamos a pedir el permiso.

words.note: poder: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.

words.en: I can't enter the attic without a ladder.
words.es: No puedo entrar al ático sin escalera.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker where you are going this morning, what you are going to do there, and what time you can arrive.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Use regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs to say what you and others do in a room.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Techo means both the ceiling and the roof.
Mexican usage for a wall light switch.
Mexican usage.
Mexican usage. Also: el enchufe.

words.en: I work in the kitchen today.
words.es: Yo trabajo en la cocina hoy.
words.note: -ar: trabajo, trabajas, trabaja, trabajamos, trabajan.
Informal tú: use it between coworkers.

words.en: You live on the second floor.
words.es: Usted vive en el segundo piso.
words.note: Formal usted, for a customer.

words.en: We change the bathroom light bulb.
words.es: Nosotros cambiamos el foco del baño.
words.note: -er: cambio, cambias, cambia, cambiamos, cambian... (cambiar is -ar).

words.en: They open the living room wall.
words.es: Ellos abren la pared de la sala.
words.note: -ir: abro, abres, abre, abrimos, abren.

words.en: We climb up to the roof carefully.
words.es: Nosotros subimos al techo con cuidado.
words.note: -ir: subimos.

lessons.speaking: Describe to a customer what you do and what your crew does in one room, using yo, nosotros and ellos with three different verbs.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask a customer basic questions about an electrical problem.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Two words, with an accent on qué.
Masculine, even though it ends in -a.

words.en: When did the power go out?
How much does the permit cost?
Why is the panel making noise?
Which is the problem? / What is the problem?
words.note: Use cuál before es to ask 'what is'.

lessons.speaking: Ask a homeowner three questions about the problem: where it is, when it started, and what noise they hear.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing, not yet, more, less and another about a job.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos, otro

words.note: Feminine: otra.

words.en: I never work with live wires.
words.note: Safety rule: test and turn off before you touch.

words.en: There is nobody in the basement.
words.es: No hay nadie en el sótano.
words.note: Spanish uses a double negative: no hay nadie.

words.en: I haven't finished the job yet.
I need more wire and another breaker.
words.es: Necesito más cable y otro breaker.

words.en: I want to use fewer extension cords.
There is nothing wrong in the panel.
words.es: No hay nada malo en el panel.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you never do, what you have not finished yet, and what you need more or less of.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Make polite requests and give simple commands to customers and your crew.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? and usted commands for everyday verbs; ustedes commands to a crew

words.en: Can you show me where the panel is?
words.note: Polite and formal. Use with a customer.

words.en: Can you open the door, please?

words.note: usted command to one person.
usted command: -ar verbs end in -e.
ustedes command to a crew: end in -en.
ustedes command to a crew.

lessons.speaking: Politely ask a homeowner to show you the panel and wait outside, then tell your crew to bring the ladder and check the label.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Spot Spanish words you already know and ask for help when you do not understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: -ción matches English -tion.
-dad matches English -ty.
-ente matches English -ent.

words.en: How do you say "conduit" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you speak a little Spanish, ask them to speak slowly, and use two cognates to say that safety is important.
